category_title: At-risk four-year-olds from low-income families with context-dependent oral language proficiency
student_description: This student is an at-risk four-year-old with delayed language development who frequently defaults to one-word responses with adults due to a fear of making grammatical errors. While they can use more complex language with peers, they uniquely require adults to actively model complete sentences, recast their short answers with elaboration, and ask open-ended questions rather than relying on compliance-based directions or low-level recall questions.

criteria.rationale: Continuous exposure to complete, descriptive sentences from adults is necessary to overcome the student's language delays and build their confidence in using proper grammar.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly includes a commitment for the tutor to consistently speak in complete, grammatically correct sentences during all interactions with the student.

criteria.rationale: The student needs opportunities to practice elaborate language structures in various settings, not just during formal instruction, to generalize their language skills.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates focused language-building experiences across both teaching-directed times (e.g., reading) and non-teaching directed times (e.g., center play).
